help.title: Help
help.qsIntro: OpenRiskSim works like Risk Simulator: mark the uncertain cells of your model and the result cells, and let the Monte Carlo simulation compute thousands of scenarios.
help.qs1: File → Open (.xlsx or .csv) or try an Example. You can edit cells and formulas as in Excel (Spanish function names such as =VNA(…), =TIR(…) are accepted too).
help.qs2: Select an input cell with a constant value (e.g. price, demand) and press Define assumption. Choose the distribution and its parameters. The cell turns green.
help.qs3: Select the result cell (e.g. NPV, IRR) and press Define forecast. The cell turns blue.
help.qs4: If two assumptions move together (e.g. price and demand), define their correlation in Correlations.
help.qs5: In Settings choose the number of trials and the seed. Press Run (Alt+R). Step shows a single trial in the sheet.
help.qs6: In each forecast window use the certainty: for example, Right-tail ≥ 0 on the NPV gives the probability that the project is profitable.
help.qs7: In Analytical tools you will find tornado, spider, sensitivity, distribution fitting and more.
help.qs8: File → Save .xlsx keeps the model inside the workbook (it can be reopened here). Export report produces an .xlsx or a PDF with charts.
help.qsTip: Your work is saved automatically in this browser. Everything is computed on your computer: no data is sent to a server.
help.aboutText: OpenRiskSim is a free and open-source alternative to Risk Simulator for Monte Carlo simulation, forecasting, optimization and project financial evaluation, designed for project-evaluation students.
help.privacy: It runs entirely in the browser (also offline, as an installable app). Your files never leave your computer.
help.gpl: This program is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms of the GNU General Public License (GPL) version 3 or later, as published by the Free Software Foundation. It comes WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY.
